label: h-initial sequence, positions 3-5, after a t/u/k/v/s context
explanation: Sparse feature (~0.01% of steps) that fires only during the original-input phase, almost always at positions 3-6 (peak t=4), and almost entirely in sequences whose first token is h (89% of mass; f gives most of the rest). It never fires at t<3, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. Within h-initial sequences it is strongly enriched when the preceding one or two inputs are from {t,u,k,v,s} (prev_tok t is 10.8x, prev2 v/k about 8x), and it favors first occurrences of the current input. The top examples (h h v t [j], h f v u [0], h h h t [v]) follow this pattern. The current token barely matters. The coarse gate (h-initial & t in 3..6) gets 88% recall but only 1% precision, and adding the context-token conditions raises precision to only ~19% at 45% recall. So the exact conjunction of earlier tokens that drives it was not captured. Magnitude is fairly flat (median 0.12, max 0.225) and is highest with h-initial prefixes such as h h ... t.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=h (+6.72), prev_tok=t (+4.60), orig1=h (+3.50), orig0=f (+3.08), prev_tok=u (+3.06), prev_tok=k (+2.99). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.24), orig_idx=-1 (-4.51), prev3_tok=- (-2.67), in_first=0 (-0.58).
